rows.sum: Battery-led revenue jump to Rs 221 cr and a swing to Rs 4 cr consolidated profit mark a clear operational turnaround, though heavy working-capital burn, rising debt and a weakening machinery business temper the headline.

CCL posted a record consolidated Q2 PAT of Rs130cr (+29% YoY) on revenue up 7.5% with better margins and lower debt, a solid, clean beat on its trend, though the standalone headline decline may confuse some readers.
SBC Exports posted record Q2 revenue (+94% YoY) and PAT (+37% YoY), but profit growth lags sales, other income is significant, and working capital and debt are blowing out.

SME textile-chemicals maker posted a 55% jump in H1 revenue and a much higher profit off a tiny base, but margins are thin, working capital and debt are rising, and profit leans on an extraordinary item and a pending insurance claim.
Q2 consolidated revenue rose 53% and PAT 91% YoY with strong pre-sales and guidance reaffirmed, a clean beat on its own trend.

LTF posted record Q2 PAT of ~Rs 973 cr (+32% YoY) on 28% AUM growth, better NIMs, lower credit costs and improving asset quality, a clean beat on trend that is probably largely expected after a strong Q1.
Solid quarter with record revenue, margin expansion and 31% PAT growth, tempered by rising leverage, negative operating cash flow and NSE returning the merger application.
5paisa grew revenue 12% on margin funding but profit fell 26% YoY and 39% QoQ on falling brokerage fees and higher costs, with EPS halved by rights dilution — a weak print.
Mahindra EPC swung back to a Rs 2.2 cr profit on 46% YoY revenue growth in a seasonally weak quarter, a decent turnaround from Q1, though H1 profit remains below last year.
Metro Brands posted a steady but unspectacular Q2 with 12% revenue and PAT growth off a weak base, with festive demand deferred to Q3, likely a neutral-to-slightly-soft reaction.
Q2 consolidated revenue fell ~13% YoY to Rs 1,527 cr and PAT shrank to Rs 17 cr from Rs 53 cr last quarter, so the 'turnaround' headline masks sequential deterioration despite a larger order book.
Revenue grew 14.5% but consolidated loss widened to Rs 208 cr as EBITDA margin collapsed to about 1% and a Rs 62 cr subsidiary sale loss hit, so the turnaround hoped for after Q1 looks stalled.
Q2 consolidated PAT of Rs 335 cr is up 58% YoY on 19% revenue growth with margins above guidance, but orders and market share softened QoQ on regulatory changes.
The seasonal Q2 tripled sales to Rs 85.9 cr but profit barely rose to Rs 2.36 cr as margins shrank, and receivables ballooned, so the stock is likely to see a muted to slightly negative reaction.
Tech Mahindra posted a clean, strong Q2: revenue up 15.6% and profit up 34% YoY with margins expanding, and it sweetened the result with a 1:1 bonus and Rs 15 dividend, so a positive bias is likely.

Strong 26.5% revenue growth and a record order book, but margins are compressing and half of reported PAT is a one-off earnout reversal, leaving core profit of about Rs 16 cr roughly flat sequentially.
Core ARR business grew strongly, but treasury MTM losses and weak transactional income pushed consolidated PAT down about 5% YoY and 9% QoQ, below the recent trend, which likely weighs on the stock.
Modest 7% revenue growth with flat EBITDA and slightly lower standalone profit; with the IHCL merger pending, the stock should track IHCL more than this quiet quarter.
HDFC Life posted steady 14% PAT growth and 16% premium growth with better solvency, but weaker persistency and higher expense ratio temper the read.

Wipro posted flat constant-currency revenue, a modest margin gain and lower net profit, but the sharp drop in large-deal bookings and soft Q3 guidance (midpoint negative) point to a negative reaction.

Heritage Foods posted 19% revenue growth and a sequential margin recovery to 5.6%, but consolidated PAT of Rs 31 cr is still down ~39% YoY on milk cost inflation, so the read is a modest QoQ improvement off a depressed base.
Butterfly posted a record Rs 331 cr quarter with 13% revenue and ~19% PAT growth and steady 9.5% EBITDA margin despite commodity-driven gross margin pressure, a solid but not spectacular print.

HDFC AMC's core revenue grew 14% and operating profit about 16%, but headline PAT rose just 4% YoY and fell 11% QoQ on lower treasury income; it is a solid core quarter that may read soft on the headline.

Orient Electric's Q2 revenue grew 25% and PAT doubled to Rs 27 cr on a weak base with better operating margins, though gross margin compression and a sequential dip temper the result; the filing came out during market hours.

KVB posted a clean quarter with 37% YoY profit growth, 20% loan growth and improving asset quality, though weaker other income and the low-provision base temper it; the filing came out during market hours, so part of the reaction may already be priced.
A clean beat: consolidated revenue grew about 10% and net profit about 86% YoY to 341 cr, helped by operating leverage and Campaign Registry, though rising debt and receivable write-offs temper it.
Tips posted a strong 35% revenue and 23% PAT growth quarter with a sharp sequential recovery and an upbeat guidance comment, though margins remain below last year's due to heavier content spending.
Weak Q2: revenue down 5.5% and profit down 27% YoY with sharp margin compression from higher newsprint costs, flattered by a Rs 13 cr one-off gain; festive timing explains only part of the shortfall.
South Indian Bank posted a record Rs426 cr profit (+21% YoY) driven by core NII growth of 38% and sharply better margins and asset quality, a clean beat on its own trend despite higher provisions.
UCO Bank posted a 27% YoY rise in Q2 net profit to Rs 786 cr on 32% interest income growth and markedly cleaner asset quality, though higher ECL provisions and flat other income temper the beat.
Polycab posted a blowout Q2 with revenue up 53% and PAT up 43% to Rs 990 cr, led by W&C and a FMEG margin breakthrough, though YoY margins slipped slightly and working capital swelled.

Indian Bank posted Q2 profit of Rs 3,462 cr (standalone, +14.7% YoY) with solid loan and NII growth and cleaner asset quality, though operating strength came partly from treasury gains offset by heavy standard provisions, so the stock should see a modestly positive reaction.
Fedfina posted a strong Q2 with 63% YoY PAT growth on 37% AUM growth and operating leverage, though a QoQ uptick in NPAs and flat disbursements temper the print.
Infollion's H1 revenue rose 16% YoY but consolidated PAT fell 8% to Rs 6.7 cr on margin compression, with weak cash flow from a receivables jump, though sequentially it improved from a soft H2.
MRPL tripled Q2 PAT to about Rs 1,900 cr on strong refining margins and cut debt sharply, though a refinery unit fire on Sep 30 adds near-term operational uncertainty.

The micro-cap NBFC posted its best quarter yet, with Rs1.51 cr profit on Rs2.77 cr revenue, but that was driven by lumpy fee income, diluted by a large share issue and clouded by an auditor resignation.
Q2 PAT rose 15.5% YoY to Rs 946 cr and recovered sharply from a weak Q1, but the beat leans on investment gains while underwriting losses persist.
Strong 29% revenue growth but rising funding costs held PAT to Rs 10.9 cr (+7% YoY, slightly below Q1), a middling quarter with squeezed margins.
Strong YoY growth driven by capacity added and lower interest costs, but sequential growth has stalled at a ~35% margin, so the result looks largely in line and the stock reaction is likely muted.

CEAT posted 26% revenue growth but consolidated profit fell 40% YoY to Rs 112 cr on raw-material-driven margin compression and subsidiary losses, a partial recovery from a dismal June quarter but still well below last year's run-rate.
Bajaj Consumer posted strong YoY growth (revenue +25%, profit +66%) with high margins sustained, though sequentially sales dipped and profit was flat.
RIIL's revenue fell 31% YoY to Rs 8.35 cr with core operations loss-making and consolidated PAT down 8.5% to Rs 2.80 cr, propped up by treasury income and a tax credit.
Acquisition-boosted 28% revenue growth and steady 16% margins, but net profit is nearly flat YoY and down QoQ, so the result reads as in-line to slightly soft at the bottom line.
Strong YoY earnings growth driven by lower provisions, but sequentially flat profit with slight NIM compression and an uptick in stage 3 make it a steady, largely expected quarter.

Leela's Q2 shows strong 33% revenue and 36% operating EBITDA growth on ADR-led RevPAR gains, with PAT up 27% to Rs 95 cr despite larger JV losses, a solid beat on its own trend that was released during market hours.
Clean Q2 with consolidated revenue +10.5%, EBITDA +18% and margin expansion led by gears plus a 33% larger order book, though PAT grew only ~10% and MHE margins slipped.
Canara Bank Q2 standalone PAT up 8.4% to Rs 5,175 cr on strong 19% loan growth and much lower provisions with GNPA at 1.33%, but weak other income kept operating profit flat at +2%.
Accent Microcell's H1 FY27 standalone profit jumped 72% YoY to Rs 31.1 cr on 25% revenue growth with much higher margins, though revenue dipped versus the strong prior half.
Revenue jumped 19% on the ACT acquisition but flat EBITDA, shrinking margins and rising depreciation pushed GTPL into a quarterly loss, a clearly weak print.

Revenue grew strongly to Rs 36 cr, but the headline consolidated profit of Rs 49.8 cr is almost entirely a one-off gain from deconsolidating the Singapore subsidiaries, while underlying pre-exceptional profit fell YoY and leaned on other income and provision write-backs.
Tata Elxsi delivered healthy 15% YoY revenue growth with a QoQ margin recovery, but net profit was flat sequentially on lower other income, so this is a solid but not spectacular quarter.
Sejal Glass posted a record quarter with consolidated revenue up 33% and PAT up 78% YoY to Rs14.4cr, driven by its foreign subsidiary, a clear beat on its recent trend.
DEN's profit edged up only because of treasury other income while revenue fell 4% and the core cable and broadband businesses deepened their operating losses.
A clean, record quarter with PAT up 50% YoY and no exceptional items, driven by MTF and distribution growth and lower finance costs, though cost growth is high.

TARIL had a clean, strong Q2: consolidated revenue rose 61% and PAT more than doubled to Rs 81 cr on margin expansion, backed by order inflow nearly doubling and guidance reaffirmed, though part of the jump reflects a weak year-ago base.
Strong YoY growth off a depressed base and a much larger order book, but profit halved sequentially, other income fell and the CFO resigned, so the read is mixed.
PNB Gilts posted Rs 44.8 cr Q2 profit versus a year-ago loss, but earnings nearly halved sequentially on trading losses amid rising yields, so the result reads mixed.
Growth looks solid against a weak year-ago base, but margins and profit fell sharply from the strong June quarter, breaking the recent improving trend, so the stock could be under pressure.

Consolidated revenue fell 21% YoY to Rs 18.8 cr and profit dropped to Rs 1.86 cr (helped by a tax credit). The networking products segment is growing, but the drop in real estate revenue and higher interest and lease costs leave the result weak.
Core AMC revenue grew a solid 16% YoY with stable margins, but weak other income held PAT growth to 6% YoY and an 8% QoQ dip, partly offset by a big Rs 30 interim dividend.
HCLTech posted a solid Q2 with 2.3% QoQ CC growth, 131 bps margin expansion and record profit plus strong bookings, a modest beat in a low-growth sector.
RBL Bank posted a big beat with profit up ~2.6x YoY on 37% NII growth, wider NIM and cleaner asset quality, though treasury gains and the fresh capital flatter the numbers and ROE stays low.
A negligible-revenue agri shell posted a wider Rs 0.3 cr quarterly loss, its assets dominated by a sub-judice loan, with a repeat auditor qualification — poor.
Small-cap chemical maker posts a sharp revenue jump and return to a thin profit after losses, though profit is largely other income and cash flow is weak.
Clean quarter: record profit of Rs 60.6 cr (+22%) on 26% revenue growth driven by strong tractor engine volumes, with flat margins and no one-offs.
DMart posted strong revenue (+18%) and better LFL growth, but margin compression held PAT growth to about 8.5%, a familiar profitability disappointment for a richly valued stock.
Premier Polyfilm posted record sales up 39% YoY and profit up 22.5%, but margins slipped to about 14% on higher material costs, so this is solid growth with some margin dilution.
Indbank's Q2 revenue was flat at Rs 6.36 cr, but higher costs cut net profit 13% YoY and 32% QoQ to Rs 1.61 cr, a weak quarter for this small stock.
Core fee revenue grew 17% YoY and PAT rose 21% to Rs 59 cr, but the sharp QoQ profit drop on lower treasury gains and weakening SIP metrics temper the read.

Can Fin's implied Q2 PAT of ~Rs 275 cr is up ~10% YoY with slightly better NIM, but 9-10% loan and disbursement growth stays sluggish, so this is a steady, in-line quarter unlikely to move the stock much.
Underlying growth is on track (adjusted PAT +22%, record inflows, AUM +18% in a falling market), although ESOP costs pushed reported PAT down 11% YoY; this is a steady result in line with guidance.
A steady quarter: Q2 PAT rose about 6% YoY to Rs 43 cr and H1 VNB grew 24% with a 21% margin, but lower solvency and a new sub-debt raise temper the read.
A clean beat-the-trend quarter: PAT up 22% QoQ to Rs375cr with falling credit costs, better asset quality and expanding NIM, though a strong run-up may already price much of this in.
TCS posted 11% revenue and 15% profit growth YoY, but much of it reflects acquisitions and a low restructuring-hit base, while sequential growth was a soft 1.3% and segment margins narrowed.
GM Breweries' implied Q2 profit of about Rs 39 cr is up roughly 11% YoY but flat on the prior quarter, a steady but unexciting print that was released mid-session.

A delayed March-quarter result whose Rs 136 cr consolidated profit comes from a finance-cost reversal and impairment write-back rather than operations, alongside a modified consolidated audit opinion and negative net worth, so it offers little fresh positive surprise for a stock already trading on the SASPL divestment story.
Delayed audited Q4 FY26 standalone results show a small profit on 34% YoY sales growth but weak full-year revenue and negative operating cash flow, which is unlikely to move this micro-cap much.
Insolvent RCOM's loss narrowed on one-off exceptional gains while revenue keeps shrinking and auditors heavily qualify the accounts, so the result carries little positive information for the stock.
Profit doubled YoY off a tiny base, but margins and profit collapsed versus the strong March quarter and debt rose, so the market is likely to read this as a disappointing QoQ reversal.

Jinkushal's Q1 consolidated profit collapsed 66% YoY to Rs 2.2 cr despite 16% revenue growth, as freight, staff costs and a heavy overseas inventory build squeezed margins to roughly 5%, a weak print for a small recently listed stock.

Revenue surged and the company swung back to a small profit, but near-zero margins and active ED, SFIO and SEBI investigations keep the stock's risk profile dominated by regulatory overhang rather than the numbers.
A defunct, zero-revenue textile group posted another ~Rs 51 cr consolidated loss with insolvency proceedings pending and interest unprovided, so there is nothing positive here for a distressed stock.
Deep consolidated loss of Rs 87 crore on large impairments and write-offs, with a qualified review, going-concern doubt and an ongoing debt default, reads very poorly despite flat toll revenue.

Headline profit is small and down sharply YoY, the remaining business after the mall sale is loss-making, and the Nagpur NOC overhang persists, so this is a weak read with the Inorbit deal the only support.

EPS of about Rs 59 versus about Rs 33 a year ago points to a strong roughly 80% profit jump that extends the March-quarter surge, partly clouded by a wholesale leadership reshuffle and an unreadable results table.
Monsoon-quarter revenue grew modestly but profit fell about 41% on fuel- and maintenance-driven cost inflation, partly offset by the announcement of a room-expansion plan.

Aksh Optifibre's Q1 numbers are not visible in the filing text, and the company is under CIRP with an NCLAT stay pending, so insolvency risk rather than earnings will drive the stock and the bias is negative.

Accounting profit is weak and leans on other income, but pre-sales jumped 5x to ~Rs 1,093 cr and the company got a first-time A+ rating, so the operating story is solid and the first-day reaction is likely balanced.

The filing text lacks the actual P&L table, so beyond a clean review and modest subsidiary profits the quarter cannot be judged; expect a sequential decline from a record March quarter against a weak year-ago base.
Revenue more than halved YoY and core operations were loss-making, with reported profit propped up by other income and a deferred tax credit, a weak quarter for this low-margin trader.
A micro-cap edtech with revenue down ~22% YoY and profit down ~65% to a token ~10 lakh, propped by other income and a tax credit, reads weak despite the sequential return to profit.
Filatex Fashions' Q1 revenue fell 57% YoY to Rs 20 cr and profit fell 78% to Rs 0.31 cr, with other income propping up PBT and gratuity unprovided, so the read is weak for this penny stock.

Revenue grew 18% but EaseMyTrip swung to a Rs 117 cr consolidated loss as air margins collapsed and costs ballooned, marking a third straight weak quarter that is likely to keep pressure on the stock.
Q1 standalone revenue fell 36% YoY and pre-tax profit roughly halved, while a restatement trimmed FY26 profits and leverage is climbing, so this reads as a weak print.
High-single-digit revenue growth but rising interest and depreciation from acquisitions pushed consolidated profit down 14% YoY, a soft Q1 likely to weigh on the stock.
A solid quarter, with revenue up about 20% and profit roughly doubling on subsidiary strength, partly offset by the sudden CFO exit, so expect a modestly positive but uncertain reaction.

Q1 consolidated growth is mostly from the Peaton acquisition, while standalone business is flat, EPS is lower YoY on dilution and the sequential trend weakened, with a secretarial auditor resignation adding a mild governance overhang.

The filing text covers only management changes, including a new CEO and CTO, and leaves out the Q1 numbers; against a weak recent margin trend, the first-session move is close to a coin flip, leaning slightly negative.
Sales jumped 2.5x YoY, but margins collapsed and profit halved to a token Rs 0.16 cr that depends entirely on other income, with a qualified auditor review, so it reads as weak.
Q1 swung to a Rs 58 cr consolidated loss as revenue fell 4% YoY and EBITDA margin halved to ~9%, with an abandoned QIP and rising debt adding to a clearly poor print.

Nova Agritech posted 28% YoY revenue growth and a strong rebound from a near-zero March quarter, but consolidated profit was flat YoY at Rs 3.25 cr as higher depreciation and costs absorbed the growth, so the read is mixed.

PAT is up ~30% on ~6% revenue growth, but the gain leans on lower depreciation after the lease exit and on higher other income, while rights-issue dilution and the ESOP cap per-share gains, so the result reads as mixed.
Blowout Q1 with PAT up over 7x YoY on film price spikes and forex gains, though management flags Q2 normalization, so a likely positive but possibly tempered reaction.

Headline profit jumped about 2.5x YoY, but it rests on regulatory income and one-off gains, the core business lost more before regulatory income, and the auditor disclaimed its conclusion, so the result reads as mixed for a volatile, governance-clouded stock.

GSS swung to a marginal consolidated profit on lower costs, but revenue shrank sequentially and the profit is negligible, so the result gives little reason to buy a micro-cap with a weak track record.

Q1 sales grew ~17% YoY and PBT ~26%, but headline profit is flattered by a prior-year tax write-back and a large unexplained Rs 56 crore exceptional gain, so underlying growth is decent rather than spectacular.
Small-cap Ambica Agar's Q1 revenue fell 18% YoY with profit flat at Rs1.1 cr, propped up by other income and dragged by hotel losses, so expect a muted, slightly negative reaction.
Tiny loss-making microcap: consolidated revenue rose sharply to Rs 2.4 cr and the loss narrowed YoY to Rs 1.9 cr, but near-zero gross margin and a wider standalone loss leave no sign of a turnaround.

The filing text carries only board outcomes and a fund-utilisation report without the actual Q1 FY27 numbers, so the stock's reaction hinges on figures not visible here against a lumpy, recently loss-making history.

Consolidated profit jumped to Rs 7.1 cr on a QoQ revenue recovery and better margins, but revenue is still down YoY and the below-net-worth sale of a subsidiary raises governance questions, so the reaction is a toss-up.
Clean quarter with ~17% revenue growth and ~71% profit growth YoY on margin expansion, but sequentially flat versus a strong March quarter, so the upside may be partly expected.
The filing text shows only clean auditor review reports without the actual numbers, so with margins trending down and a tough high-margin June 2025 base, the read is neutral-to-cautious.

Operations improved, with revenue up 35% YoY and EBITDA up 54%, but reported profit fell about 78% against a one-off-boosted base and governance flags on the Neumesh exposure persist, making this a mixed read for a small-cap.
Shanti Overseas reported nil operating revenue in Q1 FY27 with a tiny consolidated profit propped up by other income, signalling a near-dormant business despite the absence of fresh large losses.
Strong 36% revenue growth and a small core pre-tax profit, but margins compressed sharply and most of the Rs 21 cr net profit comes from a one-off land sale, so the read is mixed.
Q1 FY27 revenue collapsed 59% YoY to Rs 172 cr, with a Rs 14.5 cr pre-tax loss and losses in every segment, which is a clearly weak print following an already poor March quarter.

Revenue fell about 80% YoY to Rs 3.6 cr and the quarter swung to a Rs 2.7 cr loss, even with other income nearly equal to sales, which extends a sharp deterioration and is clearly negative for this micro-cap tile maker.
Proprietary-trading-led quarter with revenue up 43% and profit nearly quadrupled YoY, holding near the record March level, though earnings depend on volatile trading gains.

Strong YoY growth (revenue +55%, profit +51%) led by data-centre-linked Industry segment, though sequentially softer and accompanied by governance-tinged moves on fund-use change and a promoter stake sale.
Ahlada's Q1 revenue fell 12% YoY to Rs 24 cr and PAT dropped about 70% to Rs 0.17 cr, a marginal recovery from last quarter's loss but still a weak, shrinking business.
Headline growth flatters a quarter where net-of-excise sales declined and the tiny profit came only from other income, including a creditor write-back, under a qualified auditor review.
Flat revenue and a 79% fall in net profit, driven by doubled interest and depreciation plus a heavy deferred tax charge, make this a weak quarter for a small-cap steel/power company.
Revenue grew 12.6% but margins slipped and PAT rose only 9% (down QoQ) while dilution follows the QIP, so this reads as a mixed quarter with limited upside surprise.

Standalone numbers weakened, with a Rs 96 cr loss on lower income, and the consolidated figures were not readable; profitable power subsidiaries offer some offset, but a Rs 3,000 cr QIP enabling resolution adds dilution overhang, so expect a muted to slightly negative reaction.
Q1 standalone revenue rose about 20% YoY and net profit more than doubled on sharply better operating margins with little help from other income, a strong result for this thinly-covered small cap.
Consolidated revenue fell 10% YoY to Rs 10 cr and PAT fell 24% to Rs 0.97 cr; the business remains operationally loss-making and its profit rests entirely on other income, so the quarter reads weak.
A small-cap posts a sharp YoY profit jump driven by its rice bran oil subsidiary, while the core railway business is flat to down; the result reads positively but off a very low base.
USK swung to a small Rs 2.5 cr profit from a Rs 7.7 cr loss, but revenue fell 20% YoY and profit dropped sharply from the March quarter, making this a mixed print for a volatile microcap.
A modest Q1 with consolidated revenue +9% and profit +7% YoY that recovers from a weak March quarter, overshadowed by a Rs 500 cr equity-raising enabling resolution that may weigh on the stock.

A modest Q1 for this small logistics company: revenue rose 5% and profit about 12% YoY, but revenue fell sharply from the March quarter, the real estate arm is losing money, and nothing here looks likely to move the stock.
Revenue fell ~31% YoY and consolidated results slipped to a small loss on subsidiary losses, with standalone profit propped by other income; a weak print for a thin-margin agri trader.

Election-driven ad surge only lifted consolidated revenue 4.7% while EBITDA fell 18% and the loss widened to ₹12.1 cr, with a going-concern flag and ongoing dilution, so this reads weak for the penny stock.
Anik's consolidated revenue collapsed ~72% YoY while net profit stayed flat at a negligible Rs 0.23 cr, largely supported by other income, making this a weak quarter for an illiquid trading stock.
Revenue doubled, but pre-tax profit was flat as finance costs ballooned; the 68% net profit jump rests on a deferred tax credit, making this a mixed print for an illiquid small NBFC.

NMDC's Q1 standalone profit rose only ~2% YoY to Rs 2,007 cr on flat revenue as sharply higher royalties ate into stronger iron ore sales, a largely in-line, unexciting quarter with persistent receivable and contingent-liability overhangs.
Lasa remains a shut-down, loss-making company with a qualified review, going-concern doubts and large unprovided GST demands, offering no sign of recovery this quarter.
