Sales jumped but Regency still lost Rs 2.6 cr, with the result propped by a one-off creditor write-back and wrapped in a heavily qualified audit review, so there is little to cheer beyond the pending arbitration award.

Record quarter with consolidated PAT up ~4.5x YoY to Rs 64 cr on clean operating profit (no exceptionals) and much higher margins, likely to drive a strong positive reaction despite questions on sustainability.

Consolidated PAT fell to about Rs 30 cr from Rs 52 cr (about Rs 39 cr excluding last year's one-off), revenue fell about 10% and the US business weakened sharply, so this is a weak quarter despite a sequential recovery.
Strong 60% revenue growth but sharply lower margins left Ice Make in a wider Q1 loss that would have been much bigger without a depreciation accounting change, so the print reads weak.
KRBL's Q1 profit jumped 73% YoY to a record Rs 261 cr on sharply higher agri margins and doubled other income, despite a 6% revenue dip and collapsing exports, likely a positive reaction.
Kothari Products swung back to a small profit, but Q1 PAT fell ~65% YoY and earnings rest wholly on other income and associates while the core trading business remains loss-making.
A clean beat on the depressed recent trend, with 15.5% revenue growth, 27% profit growth and margin expansion led by TVs, which should support the stock unless expectations were already high.

Core plastics business delivered strong growth and margin expansion, but headline profit is down 73% against a one-off-heavy base, and the auditor's qualifications and flood disruption temper the read.

Profit recovered from a weak Q4 and is up ~8% YoY on stronger interest income, but headline revenue fell, credit costs remain high and per-share earnings dropped after dilution, so expect a muted reaction.

Indigo Paints posted a strong Q1, with consolidated revenue up about 20% and EBITDA up 40% on wider margins, though some of the 60% PAT jump came from treasury gains and management flags raw-material cost pressure.

Revenue scale-up from acquisitions and a strong order book are offset by a sharp fall in reported and attributable profit against one-off-inflated prior periods, leaving the first-session reaction a coin flip.
Solid Q1 with 23% revenue growth and ~29% PAT growth before a restructuring charge, plus margin expansion and a positive outlook, though Europe/Australia remain soft.
Q1 was weak: consolidated revenue fell 27% and profit about 21% YoY, and management blamed Middle East disruption, so a soft open is more likely than a rally.
Bhandari Hosiery posted a weak Q1 with sales down ~13% and profit down ~20% YoY, plus heavy equity dilution, so a soft reaction is likely.
Headline consolidated profit rose 21% YoY to Rs 12.4 cr but revenue fell 15% and core pre-associate profit declined, so the beat is low quality for an illiquid small-cap.

A tiny holding company posted a modest YoY rise in tea-driven profit and a big mark-to-market gain on investments, but the related-party unsecured loan proposal and thin trading make a first-day gain no better than a coin flip.

Sammaan is back in the black after the Q4 clean-up, but the Rs 243 cr profit rests on fair-value gains and provision write-backs while interest income fell sharply and lagged finance costs, so it reads as low-quality and weak despite AUM growth and rating upgrades.

Q1 revenue fell 10% YoY and core pre-exceptional profit dropped about a third as margins compressed, with the headline profit decline cushioned only by last year's exceptional charge, so it reads as a weak quarter despite the restructuring announcement.
Sales grew 25%, but the core business lost Rs 7.9 cr before a one-off provision reversal, net profit was only Rs 0.08 cr, and distillery margins collapsed, so the underlying result is weak.
Revenue grew 16% YoY but core call-center profit nearly vanished and PBT fell 44%, with net profit down 22% only cushioned by nil tax, a weak print for this micro-cap.
Penny-stock notebook maker grew sales 22% YoY and turned a tiny profit, but margins remain wafer-thin and profit fell QoQ, so little to rerate the stock.

Underlying operations improved clearly: operating profit turned positive on lower O&M costs. Headline net profit fell YoY only because of last year's one-off gain, so this is a decent but small-cap seasonal result.
AGI Infra posted a clean Q1 with net profit up ~37% YoY to Rs 27.5 cr on only 5% revenue growth, driven by margin recovery to ~35%, a decent but not spectacular print for a small-cap realty name.

Plaza Wires posted a strong Q1 FY27: revenue rose about 38% YoY, net profit roughly quadrupled to about Rs 4.5 cr and margins expanded to about 8.6%, though an unprovided Rs 11.5 cr GST dispute is an overhang.
A steady but unspectacular Q1 with 7.7% revenue growth, flat-to-slightly-better margins and 12% PAT growth, likely seen as in line for a richly valued stock.
Solid YoY growth in consolidated revenue and profit helped by acquisitions and a deferred tax credit, but standalone growth is tepid and margins are slightly lower, so the reaction is likely muted.
Sakuma's Q1 profit rose ~70% YoY to Rs 2.8 cr on falling revenue, but almost all of it came from other income in a razor-thin-margin trading business, so the headline beat is low quality.

Genus posted ~45% revenue and ~43% consolidated profit growth YoY with an Rs24,020 cr order book, though part of the profit came from a Rs14 cr fair-value gain and associate income, and the quarter was softer sequentially.
Q1 consolidated revenue fell 7% YoY to Rs 249 cr and PBT dropped about 22% to Rs 4.9 cr as kraft paper and transport weakened, only partly offset by stronger trading, so the read is weak.
A solid quarter with 27% revenue growth, firm margins and PAT up 2.4x YoY, but profit was flat sequentially and roughly matched by other income, so the stock may see a modest positive reaction.
Flat revenue with profit down about 61% YoY as thin edible-oil margins compress further, plus an independent director exit, reads poorly for this small-cap.
Dangee Dums grew revenue 12% YoY but remained in a ~Rs 0.5 cr loss, with flat losses YoY propped by higher other income, so this is a weak result for an illiquid microcap.
Tirupati Forge grew Q1 sales 18% YoY, but revenue fell 9% QoQ and net profit dropped 14% to Rs 1.22 cr, with EPS diluted by warrant conversions, a soft print likely to weigh on the stock.

Praj's PAT doubled YoY to Rs 11.6 cr on 12% revenue growth off a weak base, but core margins remain thin and about 40% of PBT came from a one-off insurance claim, so the reaction likely depends on whether the Rs 1,000 cr order intake and new data center and semiconductor wins are read as a turnaround.
Q1 FY27 revenue fell 18% YoY and net profit slipped 3% to Rs 1.27 cr, with persistent auditor emphasis-of-matter flags and related-party capex concerns, a soft result for a small, lumpy microcap.
Strong 64% YoY revenue growth and a sharply narrower loss, but the company remains loss-making with a slight QoQ deterioration, so expect a muted reaction.
Gokul's consolidated Q1 profit rose ~58% YoY to Rs 6.1 cr on 10% revenue growth, a decent print for a thin-margin edible oil trader though other income remains a big chunk of PBT.
Strong YoY growth and cleanup of auditor/legal overhangs, but revenue and pre-tax profit were flat-to-down sequentially with thinner margins, so the stock reaction may be muted.
Loss-making auto-component maker reported Q1 results without visible figures in the extract, alongside a move to raise authorised capital that hints at dilution, leaving a mildly negative bias.
Approximate figures from a garbled filing suggest revenue fell sharply from recent quarters and profit dipped year on year, a weak quarter for this micro-cap.
Sigachi stays profitable, with margins holding near 13-14%, but revenue is shrinking and pre-exceptional profit is half of last year's, so this is a flat, uninspiring recovery quarter.
A clean beat-quality quarter, with revenue up ~24%, margins expanding and PAT up ~1.8x, should be received positively, though Vapi flood disruption may temper the Q2 outlook.
Small-cap textile processor posted steady ~6% revenue growth and 18% consolidated profit growth with a clean review, but the quarter is unremarkable and illiquid, so a muted reaction is likely.
Revenue keeps shrinking (-30% YoY), a tiny profit is carried by other income, and a qualified review over a Rs 290 cr GST demand dwarfs the business, so the result reads weak.
Record quarter with consolidated revenue up 27% and net profit up 67% YoY on strong scaffolding and drum closure growth, a clear beat on the recent trend though partly aided by Rs 40 cr other income.

Flat revenue, a wider consolidated loss from JV losses, and an auditor qualification over unprovided impairments on large loans to loss-making subsidiaries make this a weak quarter for a small illiquid stock.
Strong topline but sharp margin compression leaves consolidated PAT up only 8% YoY and down QoQ, likely a disappointment versus expectations.

Q1 consolidated revenue rose 68% and profit more than doubled YoY, but profit leans heavily on other income and sales fell sharply from the March quarter, making this a decent but low-quality beat for a small illiquid stock.
Manomay posted solid 20% top-line growth and 11% profit growth with no one-offs, but margins slipped to a multi-quarter low, making this a decent but unexciting quarter for a small-cap textile stock.

Flat Q1 revenue but net profit up 52% YoY on lower interest and depreciation, plus a Rs 41 cr OCI revaluation gain on its Asian Hotels (West) stake that lifts book value; a modestly positive read for a thinly tracked stock.
Kanani swung to a small consolidated loss on 23% lower YoY revenue with razor-thin trading margins, a weak print for an illiquid microcap.

Q1 FY27 was weak: revenue fell 28% YoY and PAT dropped 80% to Rs 3.1 cr on very thin operating margins, with an unsettled Rs 6.1 cr insurance claim flagged by the auditor, so expect a negative reaction.
Revenue grew 18% but a feed-margin collapse cut consolidated PAT 37% YoY to Rs 116 cr, with other income carrying a large share of profit, a clearly negative print.
The filing text gives only the board outcome and an EPC limit enhancement, not the Q1 numbers, so the result is indeterminate against a weak recent margin trend and an easy base quarter.

Strong 75% YoY revenue growth but margins compressed sharply, Q1 profit is just Rs 1.9 cr vs a much better Q4 operating run-rate, with a flat Q2 revenue outlook and a qualified auditor review—likely a negative read.

RCF's Q1 PAT rose 35% YoY to Rs 73.5 cr even after a Rs 132.5 cr one-time retrospective subsidy cut, with chemicals strength masking a weaker fertilizer segment and a lasting ~Rs 39 cr/quarter energy-norm hit.

Revenue surged on Defence and XiDA, but a Rs 14.8 cr consolidated loss driven by deal costs and receivable provisions, along with weaker underlying Defence margins, makes this a messy transition quarter that the market may sell.
Seasonally weak Q1 shows revenue up ~9% and a narrower consolidated loss (Rs 5.9 cr vs Rs 9.0 cr) on better tea, offset by sugar weakness and a recurring auditor qualification on tax.
The filing gives no usable numbers and the tiny company has had no revenue and persistent operating losses lately, so there is little to support the stock, which is likely to trade on noise.

Shalimar Paints is effectively becoming the listed vehicle for Infra.Market through a huge swap-based preferential issue at Rs 85, which dwarfs the quarterly numbers; the price reaction will hinge on how Rs 85 compares with the market price and on how the dilution is perceived, making it a high-variance, roughly coin-flip session.

Volume metrics grew, but revenue fell 10% and profit was nearly wiped out on MICE disruption and Air competition, which is likely to weigh on the stock despite management's upbeat Q2 pipeline comments.

Consolidated swing to Rs 45 cr profit on a volatile foreign associate's earnings looks dramatic, but standalone core is weak and profit dominated by other income, so the reaction in this illiquid holding-company stock is uncertain.
Strong YoY growth in revenue (+34%) and profit (+68%) with stable asset quality, but a ~19% sequential profit decline from a strong March quarter and rising credit costs temper the read.

MTNL's loss narrowed YoY to Rs 842 cr on 26% revenue growth but widened sharply from Q4, and the qualified audit and going-concern doubt keep the stock a merger/government-news trade rather than an earnings story.

Headline consolidated profit of Rs 3.3 cr is a turnaround from a large loss, but it is carried by other income and associates, and owners' share is still slightly negative while operating revenue is tiny, so the read is mixed.

Black Box's Q1 numbers are not visible in the filing, but a large new US hyperscaler order of about Rs 1,240 crore and a possible capital action announced the same evening give the stock a positive tilt for the next session.

Q1 profit up ~52% YoY on flat revenue and better contracting margins. The absolute numbers are small and seasonally weak, and the fund-raise was deferred, which points to likely dilution later, so expect a muted reaction.

Profit grew about 11% YoY on flat revenue, but much of the PBT gain came from higher other income and the numbers are weaker sequentially, so this reads as an unremarkable quarter with a slight downside bias.
Vesuvius posted a sluggish Q2 with 2% revenue growth, about 140bp EBITDA margin contraction and a 7% fall in net profit, which is likely to disappoint a premium-valued stock.
Small NBFC posts 17% revenue growth but only 7% profit growth as leverage-driven interest costs climb and profit dips sequentially, a lukewarm quarter.

The filing text contains only the board-outcome letter with no numbers, so it gives no new signal on a business that keeps posting operating losses and relies on non-operating income; expect a roughly base-rate session.

Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to ~9.8% and PAT nearly doubled YoY on modest 5% revenue growth as the Heubach integration delivers, a constructive print though topline is soft and standalone weakened.
Small-cap EPC firm posted a clean, record Q1 with ~37% revenue and ~40% profit growth and a sharp margin recovery from the March quarter, which should be read positively.
Solid 29% revenue growth and QoQ margin recovery, but YoY margin compression, governance flags (MD property deal, IT search) and a USD 60m FCCB dilution overhang likely cap the reaction.
The filing text has no numbers beyond a recurring auditor emphasis on UoP receivables, so the trade will hinge on figures not visible here; treat it as near base-rate.

Post-demerger automotive SKF India posted a clean quarter with continuing-ops revenue up 27% and profit up 32% YoY and a sharp margin recovery from the tax-hit March quarter, though sales were flat sequentially.

IRCTC grew Q1 revenue 18% YoY, but net profit was flat at about Rs 330 cr because margins compressed and the high-margin ticketing profit slipped, which reads as a soft quarter for a richly valued stock.

SecMark grew Q1 revenue 55% YoY and narrowed its loss to Rs 0.19 cr, but remains loss-making with rising costs, while the announced amalgamation with promoter entities adds uncertainty for a thinly traded small-cap.
Revenue grew 26% but Religare swung to a Rs 47 cr consolidated loss on insurance losses, and the RBI's rejection of the demerger adds a fresh negative, so expect selling pressure.
Revenue grew strongly but profit fell about a third YoY on thin margins, and two senior managers resigned, so this reads as a weak quarter for a stock whose earnings are in decline.
Revenue grew 23% YoY but cost growth left consolidated profit up only 5% to a thin Rs 1.16 cr, a modest result likely to draw a muted reaction.

Apollo posted a clean beat on its own trend with ~21% revenue growth, 34% attributable profit growth and margin expansion led by hospitals and the pharmacy distribution business, a likely positive read though expectations for the stock are high.

The Q1 FY27 numbers are unreadable in the filing, so the key signal is promoters buying more shares via a preferential issue against a backdrop of weakening recent profits; the setup is roughly neutral for a small-cap.

Mukta Arts narrowed its consolidated loss year on year on 10% revenue growth, but the result is weaker than the March quarter, rests on other income, and carries a modified review report, so a muted reaction is likely.
Tiger Logistics grew revenue ~49% YoY but net profit more than halved to about Rs2.2 cr on severe margin compression, with other income propping up PBT, extending the weak March-quarter trend.
Arman's Q1FY27 consolidated PAT rose to Rs45 cr from a Rs15 cr loss on 34% revenue growth, lower credit costs and better asset quality, extending a recovery the market may already partly price in.

Consolidated revenue rose about 13% YoY to Rs 765 cr and profit of Rs 52.6 cr was flat QoQ as passenger rail strength offset a sharp freight decline, but the sequential revenue drop and the restatement and Firema liquidation overhang make this a mixed print.

Profit more than doubled to Rs 3.69 cr, but it was carried by other income while revenue fell 63% YoY, and the mid-term resignation of the statutory auditor is a governance red flag likely to weigh on this small-cap.

Sansera posted a record quarter with 33% revenue growth, margin expansion and 59% normalised PAT growth on surging ADS exports, with one-off litigation and tariff charges masking an even stronger core.
Pre-sales hit a Q1 record, but consolidated revenue fell 7% and profit nearly halved, with even that profit propped up by other income, so this is a weak print for the stock.

A record quarter with revenue up 38% YoY and core operating profit sharply higher on lower other income, while PAT rose a smaller 16% because of higher tax, a clearly strong print for a small-cap pharma.
Solid 18% revenue growth and better margins nearly doubled small profit YoY, but a sequential profit dip and a Rs 5 cr flood inventory loss in Q2 (insurance pending) temper the read.
Zodiac's Q1 revenue fell 15% YoY with a continued Rs 7.5 cr standalone loss, only marginally narrower than last year, so there is little for the stock to cheer.
Core steel trading revenue and margins collapsed; profit rests on other income, and governance and dilution questions argue for a soft open.

Textile revenue grew 36% and the consolidated loss shrank to Rs 0.31 cr, but the core business barely breaks even as interest and depreciation costs climbed, so this small loss-making stock gets a modest, low-conviction result.
Veto posted a solid Q1 with consolidated revenue up ~38% and profit up ~70% YoY off a weak base, though both fell sequentially from a record March quarter; a mildly positive setup for a small-cap.
The filing text has only the board outcome and a clean limited review, with no Q1 FY27 numbers, so treat this as neutral and near the base rate until the figures are seen.

Revenue grew a healthy 12% but pre-tax profit fell 13% as the implants business keeps losing money, with net profit growth coming only from a lower tax charge — a mixed quarter likely to draw a muted to negative reaction.
Kronox posted record revenue and ~16% YoY profit growth, but higher material costs cut margins and profit fell sequentially from a strong March quarter, so the read is mixed.

Moneyboxx posted a shrinking topline (-12% YoY) and a near-zero Rs 0.21 cr profit, with low reported credit costs and NPAs flattered by a sizable stressed-loan sale to an ARC, a weak print for the stock.

NGL Fine-Chem posted a record Q1, with revenue up 34% and profit nearly doubling YoY, though sales dipped QoQ and other income plus an inventory build helped profit, so the result looks good but not clean.

Steady quarter with roughly 10% revenue and PAT growth and a recovery from a weak Q4, but growth came from prices on sharply lower volumes and expansion start-ups are being delayed, so the stock is likely to react neutrally.
Q1 FY27 revenue fell 7% and profit 30% YoY as the Perundurai unit was shut by the pollution board all quarter; the unit has since restarted, but the headline miss is likely to weigh on the stock.
Strong 34% YoY revenue growth, but margins slipped sharply QoQ and thin, interest-heavy profit fell from the March quarter, so this is a mixed print for a small-cap.
Weak Q1: consolidated revenue fell 12% YoY and PAT 33% as margins shrank to 11% and UAE operations were hit, extending a deteriorating margin trend.

Q1 FY27 consolidated profit nearly wiped out (Rs 3.9 lakh vs Rs 258.6 lakh) on 8% lower revenue and rising interest/depreciation, with standalone losses widening — a weak print for this illiquid microcap.
TNPL returned to a thin Rs5.7 cr profit on flat revenue, with improved EBITDA but rising input costs and lower volumes, making for a lacklustre quarter unlikely to move the stock much.
Strong top-line growth of 85% YoY with profit up 41% to Rs 9 cr, but margins compressed and interest/depreciation are rising, so this reads as a solid but low-margin quarter.
Clean beat on trend: revenue +21%, EBITDA margin up to 36% and PAT +40% YoY after weak recent quarters, which should support the stock despite the lingering Meghalaya subsidiary dispute.
A holding company with no trading revenue this quarter and a slightly wider small loss; the stock trades on its UPL stake value, so the result is largely a non-event with a mild negative tilt.
Q1 FY27 shows revenue down 7% and profit down about 31% YoY, extending a declining trend despite a small sequential uptick, so the read is mildly negative for this small-cap.
A shut steel maker with a going-concern warning is pitching asset monetisation and a pivot to real estate and trading, but no deal is in hand, so expect speculative but weak trading.
DCX posted a consolidated Q1 loss of Rs 8.7 cr on revenue down ~54% YoY to Rs 103 cr, extending a run of weak quarters with subsidiaries burning cash, so the stock is likely to stay under pressure.
La Opala posted a modest Q1: revenue up about 9% YoY but net profit up only about 3%, with margins slightly lower and heavy reliance on other income, which reads as an unexciting, in-line quarter.
Revenue grew about 9% YoY but margin pressure from raw materials left net profit flat at Rs 45 crore, a lacklustre print with no earnings growth.

SPML posted strong YoY growth with revenue up ~82% and PAT up ~87% to Rs 22.7 crore, but the quarter was flat-to-down sequentially and the YoY profit gain is helped by a base-period exceptional loss, so the reaction is likely muted.

Revenue grew a modest 6% but rising staff and finance costs plus continuing Aceware losses cut consolidated profit about 10% YoY, and the Rs 70 cr of extra loans and guarantees proposed for the subsidiary adds to concern, so this is a weak quarter.
Small NBFC/trading company swings back to a Rs 3.6 cr profit, flat YoY, driven by volatile mark-to-market style income, so it offers little clear signal for the stock.

Revenue fell 3% YoY and profit slumped sharply from the March quarter as interest and depreciation rose. The tiny profit is carried by other income and a tax credit, and fresh debt is coming, so this reads as weak.
Weak quarter: revenue down 13% YoY with core operations loss-making, and flat net profit is propped up entirely by large other income.

Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue nearly doubled and profit more than quadrupled YoY with clean operating earnings, though margins eased from a peak Q4, making this a strong print likely to be received positively.
Capsule core improving but the API subsidiary keeps the group in losses (~Rs 5.7 cr, flat YoY) with rising interest, partly offset by a small promoter capital infusion at Rs 160.
Lancor's Q1 profit jumped to Rs 17 cr from near zero, but nearly all of it came from Rs 19 cr of other income on modest 8% revenue growth, so the headline flatters weak core operations.
Standalone revenue all but vanished (Rs 5.8 lakh vs Rs 120 lakh a year ago) and the loss widened year on year, with other income and an inventory drawdown dominating the P&L — a clearly weak quarter.
Tasty Bite posted strong 29% revenue growth but margins contracted, so net profit rose only ~8% to Rs 8.8 cr with help from higher other income — a decent but not clean quarter.

VIP posted only 3% revenue growth and a wider YoY loss of Rs 54 Cr, flattered by a Rs 12 Cr inventory provision reversal, so the turnaround story still looks unproven despite the sharp improvement from Q4.

Peninsula Land's Q1 revenue dropped about 37% YoY and the core business slid to an operating loss, with the net loss widening to Rs 7.7 crore despite a small impairment reversal, so this is a weak quarter with no visible recovery.
Headline profit roughly quadrupled, but it came entirely from other income while revenue shrank and core operations made a loss; only the capacity expansion announcement offsets this.
Revenue fell about 30% and the company swung to a Rs 9.6 crore operating loss, and the auditor again flagged going-concern doubts, so this reads as a weak quarter for a distressed ferro-alloy maker.
Strong YoY growth with consolidated profit nearly 3.7x to Rs 9.6 cr, but QoQ sales decline, rising debt and the scrapped promoter preferential issue temper the reaction for this volatile small-cap.

Consolidated revenue grew ~40% YoY on the EV business and losses narrowed on an operating basis, but the company remains loss-making, the core IT/licence business weakened, and the sharp QoQ drop is unlikely to excite the market.
Headline profit up 42% YoY but about Rs 23 cr post-tax comes from one-off SEIS scrips; underlying growth is a decent ~20% revenue with flat margins, so the reaction likely muted.
Centrum's consolidated loss widened sharply YoY to Rs 149 cr despite 8% revenue growth, with only modest sequential improvement and a small standalone profit offering limited comfort.

Coral India's Q1 profit of about Rs 4.4 cr is down ~7% YoY on a ~19% revenue decline, though it is better than the weak March quarter; this is a small investment-driven microcap with limited earnings signal.

NFL swung to a Rs 113 cr consolidated profit on 27% revenue growth, but the profit rests on a one-off Rs 117 cr prior-year subsidy catch-up while debt is rising, so the core business looks roughly break-even.
HOEC's Q1 profit collapsed to about Rs 6 crore despite higher revenue, with a one-off gain propping up earnings and the HPCL crude dispute still unresolved, a weak print likely to pressure the stock.

Small-cap edtech posts 12.5% PAT growth on flat operating revenue, with the profit gain mainly from doubled treasury income, though a claimed Rs 56 cr government order book could draw buying interest.
Seasonally weak Q1 shows modest improvement with revenue +8% and PAT +20% YoY, but low absolute profit heavily reliant on other income makes it an unremarkable print.
Scoda Tubes grew revenue 28% YoY, but rising interest and depreciation pushed net profit down about 26% to a multi-quarter low of Rs 5.25 cr, a weak print likely to pressure the stock.

Q1 core rice business strong with operating profit up sharply and revenue +30% YoY, though headline PAT grew only ~10% due to lower other income and sequential revenue fell on edible oil, making it a decent but not explosive print.

Core operations improved with ~19% revenue growth and stable ~45% margins, but the headline 29% profit rise is partly carried by investment fair-value gains, so expect a modestly positive reaction in this thinly traded small-cap.

A breakout quarter with revenue up 45% and net profit of Rs 15.2 cr vs Rs 0.7 cr a year ago; margins jumped to ~13%, which should spark a positive reaction in this small cap despite an inventory build.
Strong 65% revenue growth but gross margins compressed sharply YoY, limiting PAT growth to 19% with flat sequential profit, a mixed print for a recent IPO stock.
Singer posted a strong YoY turnaround in its seasonally weakest quarter, with revenue up 57% and a Rs 3 cr profit against a loss last year, though margins stay thin and earnings fell sequentially.

KRN posted a strong Q1 with consolidated revenue more than doubling and PAT up ~2.6x YoY on the new subsidiary plant ramp-up, with margins only slightly softer, which should support the stock despite QIP dilution.
Strong YoY revenue and profit growth on capacity ramp-up, but sequential margin and profit decline versus a strong March quarter tempers the read.

Revenue is up strongly but margins fell and profit dropped sharply from the March quarter, and the unexplained resignation of the statutory auditor adds governance risk for this small-cap copper maker.
Solid headline growth with acquisition-boosted AMB and 17% organic revenue growth, but textile margin compression, higher debt and one-off acquisition costs make it a good-not-great quarter.

Q1 shows strong YoY growth off a weak base but a sharp sequential drop, with thin margins and heavy reliance on other income; alongside a small dilutive warrant issue and an auditor change, this looks roughly neutral for the stock.
Revived contractor posts tripled revenue and a Rs 37 cr net profit versus a small loss a year ago, but other income, zero tax, heavy dilution and auditor emphasis items temper the headline.

Only the clean auditor review report is readable, with no numbers disclosed, so the read relies on trend: the low Jun 2025 base suggests YoY profit growth, but margins have been thin and the reaction is likely muted.
Headline profit up 42% YoY on 14% revenue growth, but it is carried by a government payroll subsidy in other income while core operating margin shrank, so underlying earnings actually fell.

GIC Housing's Q1 profit of Rs 10 cr is far below the ~Rs 45-54 cr run-rate of the last three quarters as provisions spiked and Stage 3 jumped to 4.49% on a flat loan book, a clearly weak print likely to pressure the stock.
Revenue grew 18% YoY and the company swung to a small Rs4.4 crore profit, but operating margins and pre-exceptional PBT weakened, so the turnaround looks cosmetic rather than operational.
Strong 37% revenue growth and improving IGAAP profitability, but the Ind AS loss stayed at about Rs 24 cr with no sequential improvement, making this a decent but not decisive quarter.
Revenue grew modestly, but consolidated profit fell 44% YoY on rising subsidiary interest costs and JV losses, with a thin order book, so the read for the stock is negative.
Small-cap scrap recycler posted a record quarter, with revenue up ~56% and PAT up ~83% YoY and a sharp QoQ rebound, though other income makes up a sizeable share of profit.
Headline profit more than doubled, but almost all of it comes from a Rs 7.35 cr liability write-back, while operating revenue halved and the textile business swung to a loss.
Mangalam's Q1 loss roughly halved to Rs 7.6 cr on flat revenue and an EBITDA close to breakeven, a sequential improvement but still a loss-making, low-growth print.

Norben Tea posted a small seasonal Q1 profit of Rs 0.32 cr on 4.6% revenue growth, modestly better than last year but untaxed and inventory-driven, so it is unlikely to move this illiquid micro-cap much.
Flat revenue and modest 7.5% profit growth propped by treasury income, offset by a growing order book, make for an unexciting quarter likely to trade neutral to slightly soft.

Q1 consolidated revenue fell about 26% and profit about 69% YoY as the Malawi subsidiaries lost money and divested estates dropped out, even though the standalone India tea business improved, which reads as a weak quarter for a thinly traded stock.

Consolidated profit rose 36% YoY to Rs 20 cr and rebounded sharply from a near-zero March quarter on refinery consolidation, though margins are thin and the auditor has qualified the consolidated review.

Indo Amines posted a record quarter: revenue rose 30% and core operating profit about 65% with margins expanding to about 14%, while headline profit grew only about 7% because last year's quarter had large other income; this reads as a clearly positive operating beat.

Execution collapsed, with standalone revenue down 47% YoY, core pre-tax profit near zero and receivables ballooning; the reported profit rests on one-off SPV sale gains, so expect a negative reaction.

DIC India posted a breakout quarter, with revenue up 25% and profit roughly tripling to Rs 14.3 cr on much wider margins, though a heavy working-capital build and negative operating cash flow temper the quality of the result.
The board approved Q1 FY27 results and appointed a new statutory auditor, but the extract carries no numbers, so this reads as neutral with a slight negative tilt from the auditor change.
BPL swung to a Rs 3.5 cr Q1 loss as non-cash intercompany interest and a collapse in high-margin brand licensing income swamped 10% revenue growth, with lingering litigation and auditor flags.
GSFC posted record Q1 sales up 64% and PAT up about 14% YoY, with a strong rebound from a weak Q4 led by industrial products, though fertilizer margins were squeezed by surging raw material costs.
Consolidated revenue rose sharply, but at low margins, and with other income weaker the group swung to a Rs 40 cr loss under a continuing audit qualification, which reads negative for the stock.

A solid Q1: consolidated PAT rose 32% YoY to Rs 96.8 cr on lower interest costs and stronger spirits and biopharma, with the NCLT-approved demerger as an added catalyst, though underlying net sales grew only about 9%.

Q1 sales rose 17% YoY and profit more than doubled to Rs 2.1 cr, but other income exceeds pre-tax profit and the quarter fell short of March, so read it as a mixed print with core operations still loss-making.

A micro-cap textile maker running at near-breakeven margins posted a quarter whose numbers are unreadable in the filing, under a recurring auditor qualification, so a neutral-to-slightly-weak session is the likely outcome.

Q1 FY27 shows a sequential bounce from a very weak Q4, but revenue and profit remain down roughly a third and three-fifths YoY with lower margins and auditor caveats, so the result is weak against last year despite a decent order book.

A blockbuster peak-season quarter: revenue up 34% and profit up 95%, with operating margin expanding even after stripping out a big jump in other income, plus a Rs 17 interim dividend, which should bring buyers.
Cinevista's filing text is only a board-meeting cover letter with no numbers, so the market reaction is near base rate for an illiquid micro-cap whose recent quarters were modestly profitable.
Atlantaa posted a wider consolidated Q1 loss of Rs 5.1 cr despite 26% revenue growth, hit by a Rs 3 cr one-off settlement cost, a sharp comedown from the write-back-boosted March quarter.

Mukka's Q1 revenue nearly tripled YoY to Rs 490 cr and PAT jumped to Rs 18.6 cr from Rs 1.6 cr on a weak base, though profit slipped QoQ, a strong seasonal beat that should lean positive for the stock.
Flat, MTM-driven quarter for this Jindal group investment holding company: profit is up about 3% YoY but offset by an OCI loss, so a muted stock reaction is likely.
Revenue doubled YoY but consolidated profit fell ~14% YoY and ~47% QoQ as depreciation, interest and margin compression bit, a disappointing quarter for a growth-priced solar stock.
Q1 revenue rose about 21% YoY to roughly Rs 664 crore and the net loss narrowed to about Rs 2 crore after a Rs 25 crore ESOP exceptional charge, an incremental but unexciting quarter.

The filing gives no extractable P&L figures, only an intra-group order, a token dividend and roughly Rs 10 crore of deferred seasonal costs, so this small sugar stock with a weak recent trend is a slightly below-base-rate bet.
Clean quarter with 23% revenue and 38% profit growth YoY and margin recovery from a weak March quarter, offset by QIP dilution in a volatile small-cap jeweller; a modestly positive read.

Touchwood's Q1 standalone revenue fell 77% and profit 71% YoY, which management attributes to seasonality; the DMRC project win partly offsets this, but the headline weakness likely weighs on this small-cap stock.

Revenue fell 5% YoY and PAT halved to about Rs 5 cr, and even that was flattered by higher other income and a Rs 5 cr depreciation cut from an accounting estimate change, so this is a weak quarter for a leveraged textile name.

NITCO posted a Rs 10 cr consolidated Q1 loss with a sequential drop in tiles sales; core YoY growth is decent, but the business remains loss-making and there is a large unprovided penalty overhang, so it reads weak.
Manaksia posted strong headline growth with consolidated PAT up ~73% YoY to Rs 26.7 cr on 28% revenue growth, though heavy other income and unallocable gains temper the quality.

Consolidated profit rose ~17% YoY on stronger IPL income and lower depreciation, but core TV advertising fell and subscriptions grew only 3%, so this is a solid headline with a soft underlying broadcasting business.

Omaxe posted a surprise consolidated swing to a marginal Rs 1.3 cr profit on 44% revenue growth, with a lower interest burden, but that profit rests on other income and the standalone business is still loss-making, so expect a modestly positive reaction.

A recently listed stainless maker posted a record quarter, with revenue up ~31% and PAT up ~80% YoY, helped by lower interest after IPO debt paydown; that reads clearly positive, though some of the growth is low-margin trading.
Tiny revenue base shrank sharply and the small profit is carried by other income and by skipping depreciation, while an undisclosed slump sale adds uncertainty; this reads as weak.
Strong 36% revenue growth but margins sharply compressed and net profit nearly halved YoY to Rs 6.2 cr, with more debt planned — a weak quarter.
Q1 revenue jumped 51% YoY and net profit rose 22% to Rs 5.1 crore with a sharp sequential margin recovery, a solid but not spectacular print for a small-cap cotton ginner.

Valiant Organics posted a sharp earnings jump with 13% revenue growth, best-in-years operating margin (~17% EBITDA standalone) and pharma turnaround, partly aided by associate income, making it a clearly strong quarter.
Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 33% YoY to Rs 4.5 cr and net profit halved to Rs 1.52 cr as depreciation surged, a weak print for a penny stock.
Flat sales and a near-breakeven core business; the Rs 11 cr profit rests on Rs 14 cr of treasury/MTM other income, so earnings quality is poor despite the rebound from a Q4 loss.

Wabag posted 21% revenue and 37% PAT growth with a record Rs194 bn order book, though profit growth is flattered by a forex gain swing and gross margins narrowed, making the beat less clean than the headline suggests.

Solid ~18% YoY revenue growth, but consolidated PAT grew only ~13% to Rs 64.9 crore and fell sequentially as raw material and staff costs squeezed margins, so this reads as a decent but unexciting quarter.

Jagran's Q1 shows healthy ad-led revenue growth and a radio turnaround, but core print margins compressed on raw material costs and reported PAT fell 8% YoY, leaving a mixed print with governance overhang.
Revenue jumped 74% YoY but the Rs 6.9 cr profit is entirely a one-off land/leasehold gain, with core margins collapsing from the March quarter, so the headline turnaround is weak in quality.

Seasonally small Q1 shows profit up sharply from a low base on 28% revenue growth, but the numbers carry no tax provision and an auditor qualification, and an illiquid small cap may see a muted reaction.

Astral posted strong Q1 profit growth of ~52% on a weak base with plumbing margin expansion despite flat volumes and a weak industry, a solid but partly expected beat that should lean mildly positive.
Cotton yarn maker SRTL appears to show strong revenue growth but only about 5% net profit growth, alongside a change in how IPO funds are used, which reads as a mixed quarter with limited upside.
HINDCON posted a strong June quarter: revenue up about 43% YoY, profit up about 70%+, and margins recovered sharply to around 15%, with no exceptional items and a clean limited review.
Headline profit of Rs 41 cr is a one-off land-sale gain masking a 19% revenue drop and a core business that is barely breaking even, so the print is weak underneath.

Consolidated revenue more than doubled and PAT rose 73% on the Netcom acquisition, with a 2x FY27 revenue target, though margins compressed and interest costs surged, making this a good but largely inorganic quarter.

Solid volume-led 19-23% revenue growth and good cash flow, but margins compressed and the headline 83% consolidated profit jump is largely a Tata Capital MTM gain, so the core read is good rather than spectacular.

Revenue jumped 42% YoY and attributable profit rose to Rs 25.8 cr from Rs 15.8 cr, but about half of pre-tax profit comes from an unrealised mutual fund mark-to-market gain, so the core improvement is real but more modest than the headline.
Q1 profit edged up 6% YoY on better distillery margins despite a 24% revenue fall, but the June fire that shut the 200 KLPD ethanol plant clouds Q2 and the result is mixed.

Lenskart posted a strong Q1: revenue up 43% (34% like-for-like), PAT nearly quadrupled to Rs 228 cr and the international business turned solidly profitable, a clear beat on trend though valuation may cap the reaction.

Standalone swung to Rs 17.6 cr profit only on a Rs 28 cr exceptional write-back, while core is loss-making with no operating revenue, a qualified review and the auditor resigning, though debt repayment and IBC withdrawal ease liquidity fears.

A weak Q1: revenue fell a third and profit nearly halved, hit by war-related freight disruption and lower pass-through realisations, with management guiding to continued low mango realisations, so the stock likely trades down.

OnMobile posted a Rs 289 Mn consolidated Q1 loss as revenue slipped about 2% YoY, other income vanished and restructuring costs hit, leaving the core barely EBITDA-positive despite the ONMO+ launch, a weak read for the stock.

The filing text shows only a clean review report and a tiny solar SPV investment, not the June quarter numbers, so the stock's reaction depends on figures not visible here; treat this as roughly a base-rate call.

Q1 shows shrinking revenue on both standalone and consolidated bases and compressed EPC margins, with only flat standalone profit, a thin order book and a delayed SPV sale, which makes this a weak print likely to weigh on the stock.
Strong 21% top-line growth and tariff parity commentary, but flat margins, rising interest/depreciation and other-income-heavy PBT keep profit growth modest at 7% YoY.
SEPC grew revenue 35% YoY but swung to a Rs 11 cr net loss on a DTA write-off, with weaker underlying PBT and continued auditor qualifications, a negative read for the stock.
The filing text shows only board outcomes (new CFO, re-appointments) and no Q1 numbers, and against a weak margin trend the default lean is slightly negative.

Big YoY jump off a tiny base but consolidated PAT of ~Rs 9.6 cr and an 8% OPM are well below the Q3-Q4 run-rate, with the new Chemdist segment loss-making, so the quarter reads as mixed despite the strong order book.

The core casino business keeps shrinking YoY, but the reported ₹212 cr loss is driven by a GST provision far smaller than the feared ₹16,800 cr demand, which likely makes the reaction mixed rather than sharply negative.

Indo Tech's Q1 FY27 standalone numbers are not readable in this filing, so with only a dividend, an ESOP plan and higher borrowing limits to go on, the reaction is close to a coin flip with a slight downside lean.

AYM Syntex swung to a Rs 8.7 cr profit from a year-ago loss, with margins near 9% sustaining the Q4 recovery, though about a quarter of the profit is a one-off tax credit and the result softened sequentially.
Q1 consolidated profit rose ~17% YoY on just ~2% revenue growth, helped by higher other income and offset by Brazil subsidiary losses, a middling print for a recently listed stock.
Revenue grew ~52% YoY, but net profit was flat at Rs 4.65 cr and fell sharply QoQ, with margins squeezed and a Rs 80 lakh GST hit, so the stock is likely neutral to soft.

Headline profit tripled YoY on 4% revenue growth and a sharp margin expansion, but the auditor's disclaimer over inventory valuation, which directly drives the margin, makes the numbers unreliable; expect a muted to negative reaction in an illiquid small cap.
The board approved Q1 FY27 results, but the extract shows no numbers, so the read defaults to a base-rate, neutral view on a thin-margin, illiquid small cap.
Price-led revenue growth of 67% failed to translate into profit: margins compressed sharply below guidance and PAT slipped 3% YoY, so a muted-to-negative reaction is likely.

Filing text lacks the actual Q1 numbers and mostly covers fund-utilisation and governance items, including a commingling flag, so with margins trending down the bias is slightly negative pending the figures.

Clean, strong Q1 with consolidated PAT more than doubling on margin expansion and reaffirmed Rs 5,000 cr FY27 guidance, though revenue dipped QoQ and the guidance implies a steep ramp-up later in the year.
Profit nearly doubled YoY on a thin ~3% net margin despite flat sales, but a large unprovided GST demand of about Rs 43 cr hangs over this small, illiquid aluminium stock.
Solid Q1 with record revenue, ~14% sales and ~24% PAT growth and better margins led by aligners, though lab segment profit weakness and slower adjusted EBITDA growth temper the beat.

Polyplex posted a sharp consolidated turnaround, with revenue up ~30% YoY and owners' profit of Rs 91 cr against a loss a year ago, well above recent quarters, though the standalone business softened and minority interest takes a big share.
Revenue grew ~20% YoY but consolidated profit fell (−16% on continuing ops, −31% headline) on lower other income and thin EPC margins, a disappointing print versus the recent trend.

Faze Three's Q1 revenue grew 8% YoY, but margin compression, a loss-making US subsidiary and higher interest costs cut consolidated profit 25% to Rs 9.6 cr, with other income propping up PBT, so this reads as a weak quarter.
PI Industries posted a 10% YoY revenue decline and 39% PAT drop with margins well below last year and pharma losses widening, though it improved sequentially from a weak March quarter.
Aries Agro posted a clean Q1 with ~16% revenue growth and ~50% consolidated profit growth on better margins, no one-offs, a modestly positive read for a small-cap.

Bata's Q1 shows modest ~4% sales growth but better margins, a 23% PAT rise (helped partly by last year's VRS charge) and a large Rs 25 interim dividend, a decent print likely to be received mildly positively.

EPACK grew Q1 revenue 34% but consolidated profit nearly halved on thin margins, rising interest and JV losses, with a continuing audit qualification on a disputed receivable—an underwhelming peak-season print.

Simplex posted ~20% YoY revenue growth and roughly doubled profit to Rs 10.7 cr on a clean basis, but profit fell sharply from the March quarter, margins remain thin and debt overhang lingers, so expect a muted reaction.
Starteck Finance posted a solid Q1 with consolidated revenue up ~39% and PAT up ~22% YoY on better core lending income, though profit dipped versus Q4 and the stock is a thinly traded small-cap.
Operations were solid, with 14.5% revenue and 37% EBITDA growth, but consolidated profit fell 30% on higher depreciation, interest and tax; the Adani Ports hire as MD may cushion the reaction.
Solid Q1 with 26% revenue and 30% profit growth to record levels, though part of the profit lift came from higher other income while core margins were roughly flat.

Decent 28% revenue growth and a tripling of PAT off a weak base, but margins are slightly lower, and the order book is heavily dependent on a related-party solar project, making this a mixed quarter for the stock.
Syncom posted a strong Q1 with consolidated PAT up ~58% YoY on just 7% sales growth thanks to sharp margin expansion, though inventory build and other income temper quality.
Revenue collapsed about 64% YoY to Rs 18.3 crore and the thin reported profit is clouded by extensive repeat audit qualifications and an NSE compliance fine, a weak setup for this microcap.
Mufti's Q1 FY27 was weak: revenue grew only 4%, while higher marketing spend cut EBITDA margin by 460 bps and net profit fell 63% to Rs2.3 cr, much of it propped up by other income.
A tiny, shrinking, loss-making company with negative net worth and a qualified review: revenue fell 44% YoY and the loss widened QoQ, and there is no positive trigger.
Revenue jumped 49% on acquisitions, but margins compressed sharply and attributable profit actually declined YoY, so this reads as a mixed quarter with mild downside risk.
Dish TV's Q1 consolidated revenue fell 19% YoY and losses tripled to Rs 286 cr with DTH bleeding and going-concern doubts, a clearly poor result for a penny stock in structural decline.
Q1 revenue collapsed 63% YoY to Rs 107 cr on few handovers, with flat profit of Rs 13 cr propped by other income, though rising customer advances and land buying support the longer-term pipeline.
Linde India grew revenue 22% YoY but margins compressed and consolidated profit slipped 2% to Rs 105 cr, with a continued auditor qualification and SEBI overhang, making this a mixed print.
A strong, clean Q1 with 34% revenue and 42% PAT growth and stable margins, though the disclosure of errors needing restatement of FY26 accounts may temper the reaction.

Headline profit more than doubled YoY but leans heavily on other income and fell sequentially in revenue, while a same-day auditor resignation and odd replacement auditor raise governance concerns likely to weigh on the stock.

Q1 revenue grew 9.5% but profit roughly halved on segment losses in hygiene and beverages, margin compression and a lease-rent exceptional charge, a weak print versus the improving trend of recent quarters.

Revenue doubled on low-margin trading, but profit collapsed 95% YoY against an other-income-boosted base, and the pharma unit is loss-making during its plant upgrade, so this is a weak print for a micro-cap.
Q1 FY27 consolidated sales fell 31% YoY and profit nearly vanished as the Bhopal plant licence issue crippled the standalone business, leaving only a token profit after last quarter's loss.
Losses narrowed YoY on 41% revenue growth, but the company remains loss-making, the train-control business has no revenue, and the auditor flagged financial stress, so the read is weak.
Flair grew Q1 revenue ~11% but margin squeeze from raw materials and lower other income left consolidated PAT flat YoY and down 20% QoQ, a soft print likely to weigh on the stock.
Flat revenue with a wider Rs 11.8 cr loss, negative net worth and a going-concern uncertainty flag make this a poor quarter for the stock despite management's turnaround talk.
Q1 profit nearly tripled YoY to Rs 158 cr on 34% revenue growth, but about half of pre-tax profit came from an unexplained surge in other income, though core operations still improved clearly.

Revenue nearly doubled YoY and the company stayed in profit for a third straight quarter, but the thin profit rests on other income and fell QoQ as Heavy Engineering margins compressed, so the reaction looks balanced.

Om Power's Q1 FY27 standalone results were filed with a clean review report, but the extracted text has no figures, so the result cannot be judged and the base-rate probability of a higher close applies.

TARC posted its first clean operating profit in a while, with revenue of Rs 217 cr and PAT of Rs 22.6 cr on Tripundra recognition plus strong presales, but PAT is down YoY against a tax-aided base and earnings remain lumpy, making this a mixed print.
Landmark Cars posted a solid Q1 with revenue up ~23% and net profit roughly doubling YoY on better margins, though profit was flat sequentially versus the March quarter.

GTL's Rs 322 cr profit is pure OTS accounting gain; the core business swung to a loss with an auditor-modified review, so the stock's reaction hinges on debt-resolution sentiment rather than earnings.
Q1 standalone PAT ₹114 cr (+5.7% YoY), helped by a lower tax rate; consolidated PAT ₹121.6 cr (+5.6%); loan growth stays sub-10% and credit costs are rising, so this is a lukewarm quarter.
Filing text lacks the actual Q1 numbers; with a strong recent trend but no visible data and no dividend, expect a roughly base-rate reaction.

Strong 44% revenue growth and a swing to a small consolidated profit point to an operational turnaround, but the profit relies on a one-off lease gain, so the result is good on trend rather than clean.
Tiny metals firm doubled profit YoY on 61% sales growth, but the quarter fell well short of the strong March quarter on both revenue and margins, so the reaction is likely muted to mildly negative.
Bafna's Q1 was very weak: sales down 23% YoY, core operations swung to a loss and the tiny Rs 0.08 cr profit came only from other income, with an unprovided GST dispute also flagged by the auditor.

AKI's consolidated sales rose 64% YoY and profit doubled off a tiny base, but revenue fell sharply QoQ, standalone profit declined, and earnings rest on other income, so the stock is likely to see little sustained upside.
Suyog's Q1 consolidated PAT fell 16% YoY to Rs 14.5 crore on 6% revenue growth as finance and depreciation costs rose, with accrued unbilled revenue and control caveats weighing on quality.

A clean quarter: consolidated revenue rose 24% and PAT 35% YoY on volume, pricing and margin gains plus lower interest, with the Saudi JV loss as a small drag, making this a good but not spectacular print for a recent IPO.
Post-merger Gujarat Energy posted a strong Q1 with consolidated PAT nearly doubling YoY to Rs 1,007 cr on a gas-trading windfall, though restated comparatives and trading volatility temper the read.

Tiny real-estate firm posts a sharp YoY jump in revenue and profit to Rs38 lakh with its first positive operating margin in a while, but the scale is minuscule and other income still props up earnings.
A solid Q1 with ~18% revenue growth and 33% profit growth YoY, though rising interest costs, an inventory build and sizable other income temper it for a small-cap.
Shilchar's Q1 shows revenue down 15% and profit down 50% YoY with margins collapsing to around 16%, a clear deterioration likely to pressure the stock.
Orient Press slipped back into a wider loss (Rs 1.25 cr) on an 18% revenue drop with flexible packaging bleeding, undoing the recovery of the last two quarters.

Steel trader Shiv Aum posted about 25% YoY revenue growth and roughly 2.5x net profit at Rs 3.8 cr, though the quarter was softer than March, and its planned BSE main-board listing is a mild positive.

Om Infra swung to a Rs6.5 cr consolidated profit on 19% revenue growth versus a loss a year ago, but it fell sharply from March, the audit review is qualified, and a large OCI hit on investments clouds the picture.

Max India's revenue grew 63% YoY but fell QoQ, and the consolidated loss nearly doubled sequentially to Rs 36 cr as senior living swung to a loss and lease-surrender costs rose, reversing the improvement seen in Q4.
Strong quarter with 57% revenue growth and profit more than tripling YoY (up 26% QoQ) with improving NPAs, though rising credit costs and leverage temper the read.
Strong revenue growth and a return to profit after a loss-hit Q4, but margins and PAT fell YoY on gas costs and trading mix, making this a mixed print for a low-margin small-cap.
TD Power posted a clean, strong Q1 with revenue and PAT both up about 72% YoY to record levels and stable-to-better operating margins, which should support the stock despite high expectations.

Headline profit is inflated by about Rs 144 cr of one-off other income, likely from the MR Organisation divestment, while core operations show 40% YoY revenue growth but a sharp margin squeeze and a sequential dip.
Weak quarter, with revenue down about 6% YoY and halved QoQ, profit roughly halved to about Rs 0.5 crore, heavy audit qualifications and a promoter stake sale, so a negative bias.

Q1 revenue appears to have nearly tripled to about Rs 303 crore and PBT rose sequentially to about Rs 12 crore, but margins stay thin and the garbled filing leaves net profit unconfirmed, so this is a cautiously positive but uncertain read.

Sales grew ~30% YoY but pre-tax profit collapsed to near zero, with the reported Rs 1.09 cr profit coming almost entirely from a deferred tax credit, so the headline flatters a weak operating quarter.

Headline profit halved YoY only because last year's quarter had a large other-income boost; underlying operating performance improved and QoQ it is a clear rebound from a loss, but the stock is thin and the result is modest.
Flat revenue but a solid margin-led profit rebound (PAT +20% YoY, +34% QoQ) plus a 1:5 split announcement makes this a modestly positive print.
Q1 FY27 numbers are not visible in this filing extract, so it reads as neutral beyond the internally funded Unit 4 loom expansion, with the reaction depending on figures not shown here.
BSL is back in profit at Rs 1.7 cr, with 7% revenue growth and margins at 8.5%, a decent rebound for a small, heavily leveraged textile maker that could draw mild buying.
